findings.claim: WP-SCP-020 §4 020H part 3 canonical adopter template uses wrong repo name (no trailing dash), creating adopter copy-paste failure and Renovate pin-bump silent-no-op risk
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020H part 3 canonical block specifies `uses: jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@<commit-SHA>` and Renovate marker `depName=jrnb2024/standards-control-plane` (no trailing dash). Actual implementation: policy-check-wrapper.yml line 41 uses `jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/…` (trailing dash present); policy-check.yml line 916 uses `repository: jrnb2024/standards-control-plane` (trailing dash present). Review instruction item (9) independently confirms the correct repo name carries a trailing dash.
findings.impact: When 020H part 3 publishes the canonical example into ADOPT-001 §12, any adopter copying from the plan will reference a non-existent GitHub repo path, causing 100% workflow-dispatch failure. The `depName` mismatch also causes Renovate pin bumps to silently no-op, breaking the Renovate-cascade contract that is a core WP-SCP-020 AC.
findings.mitigation: Before 020H part 3 lands, amend WP-SCP-020 §4 020H part 3 canonical block to `jrnb2024/standards-control-plane` (with trailing dash) in both `uses:` and `depName=`. Not a blocker for 020D1 merge (wrapper itself is correct); tracked-forward to 020H part 3 pre-publication.

findings.claim: Canonical minimal wrapper in WP-SCP-020 §4 020H part 3 omits fork PR refusal `if:` condition; mandatory-vs-optional status is not documented for adopters
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md AC item: 'Wrapper triggers on pull_request to main only (refuses fork PRs via head/base repo equality check).' Wrapper lines 39-40 implement `if: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.event.pull_request.base.repo.full_name }}`. WP-SCP-020 §4 020H part 3 canonical example has no `if:` condition. 020B acceptance criterion (viii-c) implies callers must be same-repo PRs for break-glass gates to apply, but the reusable workflow itself does not hard-enforce same-repo at the workflow level.
findings.impact: Adopters copying the canonical minimal wrapper will not have fork PR refusal. If fork PR refusal is a mandatory AC for all adopters (as the 020D1 slice checklist treats it), the published canonical example is non-compliant and will produce weaker security posture in every downstream adopter. If optional, the gap is undocumented recommended hardening.
findings.mitigation: Before 020H part 3 lands, explicitly document whether fork PR refusal is mandatory or optional for adopters. If mandatory, add `if:` condition to canonical minimal example. If optional, add it as a named hardening recommendation in ADOPT-001 §12. Either resolution closes the ambiguity.

findings.claim: Wrapper header comment cites 'ADOPT-001 §12' as conformance reference but current §12 content is 'Architecture Principles for Adopters' — the federation integration appendix does not yet exist
findings.evidence: policy-check-wrapper.yml header: 'Wrapper conforms to the canonical adopter shape documented in WP-SCP-020 020H part 3 (ADOPT-001 §12)'. ADOPT-001-project-onboarding.md §12 (line 716): heading is 'Architecture Principles for Adopters' with subsections 12.1–12.6 covering general extraction/integration principles — no federation primitive wrapper guide. The integation appendix is scheduled for 020H part 3, a downstream slice.
findings.impact: Any reader (human or agent) following the ADOPT-001 §12 pointer today finds general architecture principles, not the federation integration guide. Governance audit trail is weakened: cited conformance reference does not yet exist in the cited document at the expected content. Forward references in governance-sensitive workflow headers are a completeness gap per the no-silent-descope invariant.
findings.mitigation: Amend wrapper header to annotate the forward reference: change '(ADOPT-001 §12)' to '(ADOPT-001 §12, federation integration appendix — pending 020H part 3 publication)'. This is a one-line comment change that closes the misleading pointer before it propagates.

findings.claim: WP-SCP-020 §4 020D1 spec text '@<commit-SHA-of-v1.0.0-rc.1>' is timing-ambiguous: the tag is cut after 020D1 merges, not before
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §4 020D1: 'SCP's own repo adds policy-check-wrapper.yml calling the reusable workflow at @<commit-SHA-of-v1.0.0-rc.1>.' 020H part 1 (immediately downstream): 'Cut v1.0.0-rc.1 tag from the 020D1 merge commit.' The wrapper correctly pins at `9820489fa83f64d04f641d20e99d3933cefbb04a` (020K merge SHA, latest main at PR-open). Dispatch note and wrapper comments document the ratchet lifecycle (020D1 pins 020K SHA → 020H.1 cuts tag → 020D1.1 ratchets pin). The implementation is correct; the spec phrasing is ambiguous.
findings.impact: A future reader of the 020D1 spec row could interpret '@<commit-SHA-of-v1.0.0-rc.1>' as requiring the v1.0.0-rc.1 SHA to be known at PR-open time, which is temporally impossible since the tag is cut from the merge commit. Ambiguity about the 020D1 vs 020D1.1 ratchet split.
findings.mitigation: Amend WP-SCP-020 §4 020D1 spec text to: 'calling the reusable workflow at @<most-recent-main-SHA at PR-open time>; pin ratcheted to v1.0.0-rc.1 SHA in follow-up slice 020D1.1.' Non-blocking for 020D1 merge.

findings.mitigation: Add `docs/reviews/** @jrnb2024` to CODEOWNERS in this PR or at the quarterly bus-factor-1 escalation review (2026-07-21). Alternatively, add an explicit exclusion note in the CODEOWNERS header explaining why docs/reviews/ is intentionally not covered. Non-blocking for 020D1.
